title: bonsai.task/1
description: The task (contract §4): one unit of work, what it is, where it stands, when it is done. One markdown file per task, named <id>-<slug>.md, in the folder the workspace declares for tasks; this schema describes its YAML frontmatter as a reader returns it (JSON). Written by agents (who create tasks and set the fields agents may set) and by the studio's write path (status moves, lane changes, grants); read by Bonsai (checks, the guard, the stop gate, the ladder runner), the studio, the statusline and agents. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null or [] where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null and keeps an unknown one. The frontmatter follows the format-1 YAML rules (contract §2.4).

format.description: The version line, always the first key. A reader that meets a newer major (bonsai.task/2) says "format too new" and reads nothing else (contract §2.2). In a file made from a template the line carries a one-line pointer back as a trailing comment (contract §2.8), which is a comment and not part of the value.

id.description: The task id: T- and 4 to 6 digits, unique in the workspace; written plain, never quoted (contract §4.1).

title.description: What gets built, as text on one line.
examples: Add a dark mode switch to the settings page

status.description: Where the task stands. A closed list (contract §4.1): it never grows inside bonsai.task/1. Its line carries no comment in format 1. Who may make each move: contract §10.2.

lane.description: The lane slot (contract §6): a lane some pack in the workspace defines, or null where no pack defines lanes.

done_when.description: Checkable statements a verifier can test without having built the work; [] when none are written yet.
examples: The settings page shows a dark mode switch

depends_on.description: Ids of tasks that must be done first; [] when none.

blocked_by.description: One sentence saying what blocks the task, while status is blocked; null otherwise.
examples: Waits for the design of the colour tokens.

created.description: The day the task was created, YYYY-MM-DD, as text (a date stays text to every contract reader, contract §2.4); null when unknown.

started.description: The day work started (stamped when the task first reads running, contract §7.3), YYYY-MM-DD as text; null before.

finished.description: The day the task reached done or cut (contract §7.3), YYYY-MM-DD as text; null before.

labels.description: Everything else, as a map of label name to value (contract §5): each name is <namespace>.<name> with one dot; each value is of its definition's kind (choice or text: a string; number: a number; list: a list of strings or numbers), or null when empty. {} when the task carries none. A value of the wrong kind is a bonsai check finding, not a reading error.
